content.text: {"answer":"The supplied papers do not directly discuss why neural networks struggle to learn highly ambiguous token distributions. They focus on retrieval-augmented generation, retrieval quality, evidence selection, hallucinations, and uncertainty-based retrieval decisions rather than token-distribution learning itself.\n\nAt most, one related result is that uncertainty signals from token logits can guide whether retrieval should be used, and that token entropy may become less informative as models sharpen their predictions [10]. Another paper shows that better retrieval does not necessarily improve final answers and can even increase confident hallucinations when relevant evidence is missing [1]. But these papers do not explain the learning difficulty of highly ambiguous token distributions in neural networks.","grounded":false}
